findings.paper_title: WBC Draft AGS 2025-26 Audit&Risk
findings.headline: Housing Ombudsman found one case of severe maladministration and five service failures
findings.detail: In 2024-25, the Housing Ombudsman investigated 8 complaints relating to WBC services. Of these, there were 5 findings of service failure, 8 findings of maladministration, and 1 finding of severe maladministration. Compensation of £4,792 was ordered.
findings.matters: Multiple maladministration findings and one severe finding indicate systemic service delivery issues in housing (a material council function), with financial exposure to compensation claims.
findings.figures: 8 complaints investigated; 1 severe maladministration; 5 service failures; £4,792 compensation ordered
findings.quote: 8 complaints investigated which led to 5 findings of service failure 8 findings of maladministration 1 findings of severe maladministration Compensation ordered for £4792

findings.paper_title: WBC Draft AGS 2025-26 Audit&Risk
findings.headline: Local Government Reorganisation creates acknowledged risk of failure to deliver corporate objectives
findings.detail: Following government decision on 28 October 2025 to replace 12 Surrey councils with two unitary authorities, Waverley faces transition to West Surrey Council in April 2027. The Council has formally acknowledged that this creates uncertainty and "could potentially lead to the failure to deliver corporate objectives", and added this as a corporate risk in Q4 2024-25.
findings.matters: Organizational restructuring with a 9-month transition creates delivery risk and resource uncertainty during a critical financial period; lenders need clarity on how the authority will maintain service and financial delivery through the transition.
findings.figures: Transition date April 2027; 12 Surrey councils being replaced with 2 unitary authorities
findings.quote: Whilst the LGR and devolution ambitions could be significant for Surrey residents and businesses, in the short term, this could create uncertainty for the Council, potentially leading to the failure to deliver corporate objectives. The Council recognises this, and this risk was added to the Corporate Risk Register in Q4 2024-2025.

findings.paper_title: WBC Draft AGS 2025-26 Audit&Risk
findings.headline: External auditor recommends Council expand savings programmes to address budget pressures
findings.detail: Grant Thornton's value for money report identified that the Council should expand its current savings programmes and use benchmarking to identify high cost services. This recommendation suggests existing savings plans may be insufficient to meet structural budget challenges.
findings.matters: An external auditor's recommendation to expand savings programmes indicates the Council's current financial plan may not fully address underlying structural imbalances.
findings.figures: Current savings programmes assessed as requiring expansion; benchmarking of high cost services recommended
findings.quote: This included a key recommendation to include sensitivity analysis in future Medium Term Financial Plan development, the Council to expand its current savings programmes, use benchmarking to identify high cost services and ensure that the MTFP is aligned with all key strategies.

findings.paper_title: WBC Draft AGS 2025-26 Audit&Risk
findings.headline: Health and Safety Executive inspection identified regulatory breaches in asbestos management
findings.detail: During 2025-26, the HSE conducted a compliance inspection on asbestos management in council property and assets. The inspection identified minor breaches of the Control of Asbestos Regulations 2012 relating to administrative records, prompting a Notification of Contravention and requiring an improvement plan to achieve compliance by end of June 2026.
findings.matters: Regulatory non-compliance in health and safety, particularly around material management in council assets, exposes the authority to enforcement action and liability.
findings.figures: Minor breaches identified; compliance deadline end of June 2026
findings.quote: This identified minor breaches of the Control of Asbestos Regulations 2012 relating to administrative records. These did not place the health and safety of employees or other persons at direct risk and in accordance with the HSE enforcement management model, a Notification of Contravention was issued to the Council requesting action to ensure compliance.

findings.paper_title: WBC Draft AGS 2025-26 Audit&Risk
findings.headline: Water quality audit assigned Limited Assurance with significant safety risks in legionella and water management
findings.detail: An internal audit in September 2025 evaluated the Council's compliance with water safety obligations across its residential housing portfolio. The audit identified 5 High and 10 Medium priority actions and concluded with a Limited Assurance rating, finding significant risks in the Council's statutory responsibilities for legionella and water management.
findings.matters: A Limited Assurance rating on critical infrastructure safety indicates material control weaknesses that create operational and compliance risk, and the housing portfolio is a direct asset generating value.
findings.figures: 5 High and 10 Medium priority actions; overall Limited Assurance rating
findings.quote: The audit identified 5 High and 10 Medium priority actions and concluded with an overall Limited Assurance rating. The review found significant risks in the Council's statutory responsibilities for legionella and water management, requiring a structured action plan to address the identified gaps.

findings.paper_title: WBC - Internal Audit Annual Conclusion 2025 -26
findings.headline: Tree management remedial work backlog stands at 461 unallocated jobs, with 212 more than six months overdue
findings.detail: The audit identified 461 tree remedial works jobs awaiting allocation, of which 212 (46%) are more than six months overdue. The Tree and Woodland Policy has not been reviewed since April 2022 despite requiring annual review. Record-keeping gaps exist across inspections and remedial work documentation. There is no consistent process for notifying the Tree Team when land the council is responsible for changes, and only one of 37 zones identified as tree-free in 2018-19 has been re-checked to confirm status.
findings.matters: Unaddressed tree safety work creates public liability exposure for the council. The management of 11,306 trees is critical infrastructure maintenance, and extended delays indicate either resource constraints or governance breakdown affecting statutory duty performance.
findings.figures: 11,306 trees on management system, 461 unallocated remedial jobs, 212 over six months overdue, tree policy dated 01/04/2022
findings.quote: 461 individual overdue remedial works jobs had yet to be allocated, with 212 (46%) more than six months overdue

findings.paper_title: WBC - Internal Audit Annual Conclusion 2025 -26
findings.headline: Over 400 water safety remedial actions are overdue in the council's 695-dwelling housing stock, with 219 high-risk items and 72 outstanding over 12 months
findings.detail: The audit found 658 overdue remedial actions in tracking systems (53.9% of total tracked actions), with water safety compliance testing confirming 404 genuinely overdue. Of these, 219 are designated high-risk, including 72 that have been outstanding for over 12 months. Additionally, 164 remedial actions have no documented follow-up and 247 lack an assigned responsible party. The Legionella Policy and Management Plan are past their review dates with no confirmed completion timeline.
findings.matters: Waverley manages water systems subject to regulatory control under social housing standards. Extended delays on high-risk remedial actions expose the council to regulatory enforcement action, tenant claims, and potential financial penalties from the Regulator of Social Housing.
findings.figures: 658 overdue actions (53.9%), 404 remedial actions remained overdue, 219 high-risk, 72 outstanding over 12 months, 164 entries with no follow-up, 247 actions with no responsible party assigned
findings.quote: 404 remedial actions remained overdue, 219 of which were high-risk, with 72 outstanding for over 12 months

findings.paper_title: Approach to the Appointment of an External Auditor for West Surrey Council
findings.headline: New unitary council may achieve audit fee savings exceeding £1.8 million annually versus combined legacy council costs
findings.detail: The eleven legacy councils' combined annual audit scale fees total £2,692,786. Published scale fees for recently formed unitaries in Northamptonshire and Cumbria range from £725,000 to £822,000, suggesting material savings for West Surrey.
findings.matters: Audit fee savings represent material operational cost reduction that could improve financial flexibility if sustained.
findings.figures: Combined legacy fees: £2,692,786; new unitary comparison: £725,000 to £822,000
findings.quote: Published scale fees for recently formed new unitary councils in Northamptonshire and Cumbria range from £725,000 to £822,000, suggesting that a saving may be achievable for West Surrey Council based on existing fees.

findings.paper_title: Approach to the Appointment of an External Auditor for West Surrey Council
findings.headline: S151 Officer warns West Surrey will face very challenging financial environment from vesting day with limited resources
findings.detail: The Interim S151 Officer states that West Surrey will operate in a very challenging financial environment from 2027/28 with significant budgetary pressures, limited resources, increasing service demand and costs, reducing government funding, and greater reliance on Council Tax. She emphasises that spending must not exceed available resources.
findings.matters: The outgoing s151 is placing on record her assessment that the new authority faces tight financial constraints. Limited resources with rising service costs indicate constrained flexibility and possible pressure on service delivery.
findings.figures: Vesting day: 31 March 2027
findings.quote: West Surrey Council will operate in a very challenging financial environment, with significant budgetary pressures and limited financial resources from 2027/28 (Vesting Day), coupled with increasing demand and costs of service delivery, and reducing government funding.

findings.paper_title: Approach to the Appointment of an External Auditor for West Surrey Council
findings.headline: Finance team must retain adequate capacity to support audit process and achieve unqualified opinion
findings.detail: The workforce commentary explicitly flags that West Surrey Council must retain sufficient capacity within its finance function to adequately service external audit, respond to auditor queries, and achieve unqualified outcome. This signals audit resource capacity is a potential constraint.
findings.matters: Finance team capacity constraints have been identified as a factor in the national audit backlog. Insufficient capacity could impair audit timeliness and quality.
findings.figures: None
findings.quote: West Surrey Council will need to ensure that it retains capacity within its finance function to adequately service the external audit of its accounts and respond to auditor queries to achieve an unqualified audit opinion.

findings.paper_title: Approach to the Appointment of an External Auditor for West Surrey Council
findings.headline: Seven District and Borough Councils in Surrey have published disclaimed audit opinions for 2024/25
findings.detail: Within Surrey, only the County Council and four District and Borough councils achieved unqualified audited accounts for 2024/25. Seven District and Borough Councils have published disclaimed audit opinions, indicating unresolved audit issues in the predecessor councils that West Surrey will inherit.
findings.matters: Disclaimed audit opinions indicate unresolved audit uncertainties. West Surrey will inherit these audit challenges and must demonstrate improved outcomes.
findings.figures: Seven councils with disclaimed audit opinions; four with unqualified opinions
findings.quote: Within Surrey, the County Council and four District and Borough councils have published unqualified audited accounts for 2024/25 by the backstop deadline of 27 February 2026 and seven District and Borough Councils have published disclaimed audit opinions.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 - Waverley Q4 2025-26 Strategic Risk Register - Finalised
findings.headline: Macroeconomic volatility is forcing re-phasing or deferral of the capital programme
findings.detail: New risk in Q1 2026/27. Global instability is driving sustained volatility in energy, inflation, interest rates, and supply chains. The council flags this creates risk that 'current financial assumptions, the capital programme and housing delivery trajectories could become increasingly uncertain, unaffordable or undeliverable'. The register explicitly states capital investment 'could require re-phasing or deferral'.
findings.matters: A lender needs to know whether capital plans are at risk of material revision; deferrals or re-phases signal either financial stress or constrained delivery on strategic priorities.
findings.figures: Residual risk 9 (Moderate impact, Possible likelihood); Gross risk 12 (Moderate impact, More than likely likelihood). New risk baseline Q1 2026/27.
findings.quote: Global instability arising from conflict is driving sustained volatility in energy markets, inflation, interest rates and supply chains, creating a risk that current financial assumptions, the capital programme and housing delivery trajectories could become increasingly uncertain, unaffordable or undeliverable.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 - Waverley Q4 2025-26 Strategic Risk Register - Finalised
findings.headline: Governance of charitable trusts is failing; financial liabilities and compliance are unquantified
findings.detail: Waverley holds interests in various charitable trusts with inadequate governance arrangements. Two charities (Shottermill and Joseph Ewart) have accounts filing deadlines that are overdue (76 days overdue as of the register, revised deadline mid-May 2026). The council explicitly states 'financial risks and liabilities not being well understood' and acknowledges potential non-compliance with statutory reporting requirements. The risk direction of travel is UP, with residual risk score Significant (4) × More than likely (4) = 16.
findings.matters: Undisclosed or unquantified liabilities create contingent exposure; a lender needs assurance that all financial obligations connected to the council have been identified and are being managed.
findings.figures: Two charities overdue on accounts filing (76 days overdue, revised mid-May 2026); residual risk score 16; direction of travel UP (deteriorating).
findings.quote: Inadequate governance arrangements pose several risks, including the council's objectives and interests not being best served, financial risks and liabilities not being well understood, and potential non-compliance with legislative requirements, such as statutory reporting and the filing of accounts.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 - Waverley Q4 2025-26 Strategic Risk Register - Finalised
findings.headline: West Surrey merger creates uncertainty over Waverley's budget sustainability from 2027/28 onwards
findings.detail: Waverley has achieved an unprecedented two-year balanced budget through to February 2027. However, from 2027/28 the council merges into West Surrey unitary authority. The register confirms 2027/28 will show a balanced Waverley budget 'but will only form part of the new authority's first budget'. The crucial flag: overall West Surrey could face a deficit budget if pressures from other constituent councils (particularly Woking) materialize without government debt relief.
findings.matters: A lender needs to understand financial stability post-merger; a deficit in the combined West Surrey authority could constrain Waverley's access to resources or influence over budget decisions even if its standalone position is sound.
findings.figures: Two-year balanced budget to 2027/28; baseline budget for West Surrey shortfall produced March 2026.
findings.quote: Pressures from the other constituent authorities on West Surrey could lead to a deficit budget overall, if government debt relief for Woking Borough Council is not forthcoming.

findings.paper_title: 2025-26 Final Outturn Financial Monitoring report WBC
findings.headline: Void homes Council Tax liability was underestimated by more than 100%, with actual costs of £0.25m against budget of £0.12m requiring 2026/27 rebase
findings.detail: Council Tax charges on void dwellings exceeded budget by £0.1m, with actual costs running at £0.25m compared to £0.12m budgeted. Budget has now been reset to reflect this new baseline, suggesting either rising void rates or longer void periods than anticipated.
findings.matters: Large forecasting miss indicates either increasing housing voids (demand/property quality issue) or poor void management processes. For an HRA this is material to debt service and reserves planning.
findings.figures: Actual £0.25m vs budget £0.12m; £0.1m overspend noted in variance commentary
findings.quote: a £0.1m overspend on Council Tax for void homes (actual £0.25m vs £0.12m budget). The budget has now been realigned to £0.25m for 2026/27.

findings.paper_title: 2025-26 Final Outturn Financial Monitoring report WBC
findings.headline: Business rates charges overran by £0.2m in 2025/26, requiring budget adjustment in 2026/27 to address ongoing higher property cost pressures
findings.detail: Increased business rates charges across the year, primarily affecting commercial services, created £0.2m overspend. The council acknowledged this as an emerging pressure and realigned 2026/27 budgets accordingly, suggesting further increases are expected.
findings.matters: Rising property cost pressures reduce the council's financial flexibility and indicate wider inflationary headwinds in the local economy. Important for forecasting future cost base.
findings.figures: £0.2m overspend in 2025/26 primarily in Commercial services
findings.quote: At outturn an overspend of £0.2m has arisen due to increased Business Rates charges for 2025/26, of which the majority sits within Commercial services. This pressure has been addressed within the 2026/27 budget setting process.

findings.paper_title: 2025-26 Final Outturn Financial Monitoring report WBC
findings.headline: Waverley Training Services reporting £0.2m income shortfall with three-year business plan required to address ongoing deficit
findings.detail: Service generated only £0.2m income against £0.4m budget; mitigation through vacancies and cost cuts reduced headline variance to £0.1m, but a three-year recovery plan is now in place with results to be monitored through 2026/27. This indicates a structurally unprofitable service line.
findings.matters: A council service that chronically underperforms income targets requires ongoing subsidy and carries default risk if recovery plan fails. Important indicator of portfolio management weakness.
findings.figures: £0.2m income shortfall against £0.4m budget; £0.1m net variance after mitigation
findings.quote: Waverley Training Services is reporting an outturn income shortfall of £0.2m against a budget of £0.4m. However, mitigation measures—including vacancy savings and wider cost reductions—have reduced the overall net variance to £0.1m. A three-year business plan has been introduced to address the ongoing deficit, and progress will continue to be monitored throughout 2026/27.

findings.paper_title: 2025-26 Final Outturn Financial Monitoring report WBC
findings.headline: Cranleigh Leisure Centre capital project £11.7m behind, actively seeking additional funding with significant reprofiling into next three years
findings.detail: Project delays have occurred while additional funding is sought, with planned expenditure now reprofiled across the next three years. This indicates either project scope/costs have escalated beyond original business case or the funding model is inadequate. Represents material capital delivery risk.
findings.matters: Large project overspends and funding gaps signal poor project control or scheme viability issues. The council is unable to deliver major capital projects on time or within original funding envelope, which affects debt service planning.
findings.figures: £11.7m underspend in 2025/26; reprofiled into next three years
findings.quote: £11.7m relates to the Cranleigh Leisure Centre project, where delays have occurred while additional funding is sought. As a result, a significant proportion of the previously planned expenditure will now be carried reprofiled into next three years.

findings.paper_title: 2025-26 Final Outturn Financial Monitoring report WBC
findings.headline: Staffing underspend of £2.4m reflects ongoing recruitment and retention crisis across hard-to-fill posts, worsening as Local Government Reorganisation uncertainty increases
findings.detail: Establishment budget underspends do not indicate overstaffing but rather inability to fill posts due to market competition, skills shortages, and deliberate vacancies pending shared services with Guildford. LGR uncertainty is further exacerbating staff turnover risk. This masks a genuine resource constraint.
findings.matters: Chronic understaffing reduces the council's capacity to deliver services and manage complex transformations like LGR. Lenders need to understand whether service quality is at risk due to staffing gaps.
findings.figures: £2.4m underspend (£1.7m General Fund, £0.7m HRA); ongoing challenges flagged as key risk area for 2026/27
findings.quote: ongoing challenges in recruitment and retention across a number of roles, arising from wider market conditions, skills shortages, and competition for experienced staff. Consequently, budgets have not been fully utilised during the reporting period, despite continued service demand and the need to maintain established staffing levels.

findings.committee: Landlord Services Advisory Board (Executive Working Group)
findings.paper_title: LSAB - HRA Outturn 2526
findings.headline: Capital programme delays are reprofiling £4.6m of the new development programme from 2025/26 into future years
findings.detail: The HRA capital programme shows a total underspend of £3.8m, with the new development programme recording an £8.1m underspend of which £4.6m is being carried forward. The paper attributes this to delivery delays rather than reduced programme ambition.
findings.matters: Capital programme delays of this scale can indicate planning, procurement or execution risks that may affect the council's ability to deliver housing targets and may impact future year budgets.
findings.figures: £3.8m total underspend; £8.1m new development underspend; £4.6m reprofiled to future years
findings.quote: Within this, the new development programme shows an £8.1m underspend, with £4.6m to be reprofiled into future years. This reflects delays in delivery rather than a reduction in overall programme ambition.

findings.committee: Landlord Services Advisory Board (Executive Working Group)
findings.paper_title: LSAB - HRA Outturn 2526
findings.headline: Council Tax costs on void properties more than doubled budget at £248k, requiring 2026/27 budget increase to £250k
findings.detail: Expenditure on Council Tax for void properties totalled £248k against a budget of £115k, reflecting both the number of void properties and the time taken to return homes to use. The budget has been reviewed and increased to £250k in 2026/27.
findings.matters: This is a significant overspend that indicates either void rate underestimation or slower void turnaround than planned, both affecting housing supply targets and revenue forecasting accuracy.
findings.figures: £248k actual vs £115k budget; budget increased to £250k for 2026/27
findings.quote: A more significant pressure was seen in relation to Council Tax on void properties, where expenditure totalled £248k against a budget of £115k.

findings.committee: Landlord Services Advisory Board (Executive Working Group)
findings.paper_title: LSAB - HRA Outturn 2526
findings.headline: Staffing vacancies of £744k are masking service delivery pressures and risks to asset management and development priorities
findings.detail: The HRA has a £744k underspend due to difficulties recruiting to posts, particularly in technical and specialist housing roles, reflecting wider sector labour market challenges. While this improves the financial position, the paper explicitly flags that sustained vacancies present risks to service quality, tenant experience, and timely delivery of strategic priorities including asset management and development objectives.
findings.matters: Service delivery risks and understaffing indicate the council may lack capacity to execute its housing strategy, which affects operational resilience and borrowing risk assessment.
findings.figures: £744k underspend on staffing
findings.quote: Whilst this has generated a financial saving in-year, it has implications for service delivery, including slower progress on planned work programmes and reduced capacity to deliver service improvements.

findings.paper_title: Appendix TM2 - Treasury Management Strategy Final
findings.headline: General Fund capital expenditure forecast to drop 85% from £20.1m to £3m in 2027-28
findings.detail: General Fund capital spending is planned at £20.1m in 2026-27 but forecast to fall sharply to £3m in 2027-28, remaining at that level through 2028-29. The strategy does not explain the reason for this material reduction, which follows higher spending of £18.7m in 2025-26.
findings.matters: A sudden 85% drop in capital investment may indicate capital constraints, completion of major schemes, or reduced service investment capacity. Without explanation, it signals financial pressure that lenders would want to understand.

findings.paper_title: Appendix TM2 - Treasury Management Strategy Final
findings.headline: Capital receipts (from asset sales) have collapsed from £16.1m to £1.7m
findings.detail: Capital receipts fell 89% from £16.1m in 2025-26 to just £1.7m forecast for 2026-27, with only modest recovery to £4.2m in later years. With total capital expenditure of £37.3m but only £1.7m in capital receipts, the council must fund £35.6m from internal resources, internal borrowing, or other sources.
findings.matters: Capital receipts are a key non-borrowed funding source. Their collapse forces councils to fund capital through borrowing or reserve drawdown, increasing debt service costs and reducing financial flexibility for future investment.

findings.paper_title: Appendix TM2 - Treasury Management Strategy Final
findings.headline: HRA financing costs rising to consume 46% of rental income by 2027-28, up from 38%
findings.detail: Housing Revenue Account must pay financing costs (interest and debt repayment) rising from £13.3m to £16.4m annually. Measured as a share of net rental income, these costs rise from 38% to 46% across the forecast period, leaving only 54% of rent income available for housing maintenance and services.
findings.matters: The HRA is self-financing from rents. Rising financing costs relative to rental income indicate the housing debt burden is growing relative to available revenue, signalling potential constraints on stock investment and service viability.
findings.quote: Housing Revenue Account 38% 41% 44% 46% 46%

findings.paper_title: Appendix TM2 - Treasury Management Strategy Final
findings.headline: Capital programme increasingly financed from reserves via internal borrowing, not external debt
findings.detail: Internal borrowing surges to £24.2m in 2026-27, funding 65% of the £37.3m capital expenditure. External borrowing remains zero. This reflects a strategy to avoid market borrowing due to low treasury returns, meaning the council is drawing down reserves and cash to fund capital rather than borrowing.
findings.matters: Lenders need to understand whether councils can fund capital from their own resources or must access debt markets. Drawing down reserves to this extent constrains financial flexibility and signals potential capital funding pressures ahead.
findings.figures: Internal borrowing: £7.5m (2024-25, 33% of capex), £11.7m (2025-26), £24.2m (2026-27, 65% of capex); external borrowing zero throughout.
findings.quote: This strategy is prudent as treasury management investment returns are low and counterparty risk is still uncertain.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 7a - Section 25 Report
findings.headline: Commercial property income is robust and significantly outperforming peer councils
findings.detail: Commercial income from property investments has 'held up well' and was 'stress tested' through the pandemic with strong results. The report notes this is 'a much better position than in many other Councils' and reflects the quality of tenancies. This is a material income diversification away from government funding.
findings.matters: Strong commercial property performance provides revenue resilience and reduces reliance on government grants during a period of national funding uncertainty and reorganisation.
findings.figures: None quantified
findings.quote: Commercial income from our property investments have held up well as they are largely geared towards small industrial sectors. The pandemic effectively "stress tested" our investments and they have performed well. This is a much better position than in many other Councils

findings.paper_title: Appendix 7a - Section 25 Report
findings.headline: Staff recruitment and retention risk elevated due to LGR uncertainty, especially among experienced professionals
findings.detail: The report identifies that LGR uncertainty 'may be increased difficulty in recruitment and the retention of staff, especially professional experienced staff.' This is being mitigated with increased HR support, but the risk remains during a period when financial controls and service delivery are critical.
findings.matters: Loss of experienced finance and administrative staff during transition could impair financial controls, audit readiness, and service continuity at a critical time.
findings.figures: None provided
findings.quote: Due to uncertainty as we head toward LGR there may be increased difficulty in recruitment and the retention of staff, especially professional experienced staff.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 7a - Section 25 Report
findings.headline: Significant uncertainty about new unitary council's financial health due to proposed partner councils' financial circumstances
findings.detail: The Section 151 Officer identifies that there is 'significant uncertainty beyond the 2026-27 budget due to the formation of the new unitary council and the existing financial circumstances of our proposed partners.' The new council's starting position depends on the health of all merging authorities.
findings.matters: A weak partner council could constrain the new entity's finances, affect its credit rating, and limit financial flexibility. Lenders need visibility on who else is in the merged authority.
findings.figures: None provided
findings.quote: There is currently significant uncertainty beyond the 2026-27 budget due to the formation of the new unitary council and the existing financial circumstances of our proposed partners.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 7a - Section 25 Report
findings.headline: LGR transition costs are being borne by existing councils and built into 2026-27 budget, with risk of overspend
findings.detail: The cost of implementing the Local Government Reorganisation is not centrally funded; it is split among the existing councils. Waverley's share has been built into the 2026-27 budget. The Section 151 Officer flags that the new Voluntary Joint Committee must closely monitor transition costs to avoid overspends that would impact the current council's finances.
findings.matters: Unbudgeted LGR cost overruns would squeeze Waverley's 2026-27 budget at the worst possible moment—immediately before the transition.
findings.figures: Built into 2026-27 budget
findings.quote: The cost of LGR implementation is being met by the existing Councils. The share for Waverley has been built into the 2026-27 budget. It is important that the new Voluntary Joint Committee closely monitors the transition costs to ensure value for money is delivered and avoid overspends which would impact the existing Councils.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 7a - Section 25 Report
findings.headline: Local Government Reorganisation creates requirement for future savings to keep the new unitary council solvent
findings.detail: Two new unitary councils are forming in Surrey from April 1, 2027 (confirmed by government October 2025). The Section 151 Officer explicitly states that future savings will be required for the successor authority to remain solvent. This represents the most material near-term structural change facing the council.
findings.matters: A major structural reorganisation with required future savings materially affects credit risk and financial sustainability. Lenders need to understand the new council's financial starting position and the savings gap they will face.
findings.figures: April 1 2027; October 2025 confirmation
findings.quote: Future savings will be required to ensure the new council remains solvent and can take advantage of the transformation opportunities

findings.paper_title: General Fund Budget Setting Report 202627 (WBC)
findings.headline: MTFP projects ongoing financial pressures through 2029/30, with detailed risks in Section 25 report not provided
findings.detail: The document states the MTFP covering years to 2029/30 'continues to project future financial pressures,' but the S151 Officer's detailed Section 25 risk assessment (Appendix 7) is not included. This signals the council recognizes medium-term structural challenges beyond 2026/27.
findings.matters: Ongoing structural pressures to 2030 indicate the 2026/27 balance is temporary; Local Government Reorganisation in 2027/28 creates additional uncertainty
findings.figures: MTFP extends to 2029/30; LGR transition costs £797,783 in 2026/27
findings.quote: While the Council has managed to respond to the financial challenges in recent years, the latest MTFP for the years ending 2029/30 continues to project future financial pressures.

findings.paper_title: General Fund Budget Setting Report 202627 (WBC)
findings.headline: Pension back-funding changed from fixed sum to percentage of payroll, adding £340k ongoing cost
findings.detail: A structural change to how pension back-funding is calculated—moving from a fixed annual sum to a percentage based on payroll—creates an additional £340k budget requirement. This is set by Surrey Pension Fund and represents a loss of cost predictability.
findings.matters: This is a recurring structural cost tied to payroll growth; the council no longer controls pension funding exposure through fixed payments
findings.figures: £340k additional budget requirement from pension formula change
findings.quote: Following a change in how the back funded element of pension payments from a fixed sum to a percentage change based on the payroll, there is an additional budget requirement of £340k.

findings.paper_title: General Fund Budget Setting Report 202627 (WBC)
findings.headline: Treasury management income declining £444k in 2026/27 plus further £300k reduction in 2027/28
findings.detail: Investment income is forecast to fall £444k in 2026/27 and a further £300k in 2027/28, driven by both reduced cash available for investment and declining interest rates. This creates recurring budget pressure.
findings.matters: A combined £744k income reduction over two years represents ongoing budget pressure; interest rate assumptions about future income are material to budget stability
findings.figures: £444k reduction in 2026/27; £300k further reduction in 2027/28
findings.quote: The treasury management income budget will be reduced by £444k in 2026/27, followed by a further £300k reduction in 2027/28.

findings.paper_title: General Fund Budget Setting Report 202627 (WBC)
findings.headline: Business Rate Reserve drawn down from £2.7m to £221k after risk reassessment
findings.detail: The council reduced its Business Rate Reserve from £2.7 million to £221k after reassessing S31 timing and deficit spreading risks. The £2.48m released is being transferred to a Local Government Reorganisation reserve. This is material depletion of a buffer reserve.
findings.matters: While reassessment may justify the reduction, it removes a buffer for unexpected business rates volatility and limits flexibility for future pressures
findings.figures: Business Rate Reserve reduced from £2.7m to £221k; £2.48m transferred to LGR reserve
findings.quote: The Business Rate Reserve for S31 timing & deficit spreading has been reduced from £2.7m down to £221k. This reserve was increased particularly over the covid period due to new regulations for surplus and deficit spreading and the uncertainty on the impact this may have.

findings.paper_title: General Fund Budget Setting Report 202627 (WBC)
findings.headline: £2.2m Extended Producer Responsibility waste income forecast as one-off due to future funding uncertainty
findings.detail: The council budgeted £2,246,637 from the EPR scheme in 2026/27 for waste management, but explicitly treats this as one-off income because future funding levels are uncertain. The spend and income are cost-neutral, but future years' budget cannot assume this income will continue.
findings.matters: A material income stream (£2.2m) cannot be relied on for future years; budgets beyond 2026/27 lose this funding source
findings.figures: £2,246,637 anticipated EPR income in 2026/27
findings.quote: This is forecast within the MTFP as a one-off currently, due to the uncertainty of future funding levels.

findings.paper_title: General Fund Budget Setting Report 202627 (WBC)
findings.headline: Homelessness budget increased by £402k due to growing temporary accommodation costs
findings.detail: The council faces £402k of unavoidable growth in homelessness budgets for 2026/27, required to align with new government funding settlement and increases in temporary accommodation. This is part of £895k total unavoidable growth and represents a structural pressure, not a one-off.
findings.matters: Rising homelessness costs are a structural demand pressure that will recur and likely grow; this signals ongoing budget pressure beyond 2026/27
findings.figures: £402k increase in homelessness budget; total unavoidable growth £895k
findings.quote: A significant portion of this growth is due to the £402k increase to Homelessness budget required to align to new funding settlement and increases in temporary accommodation.

findings.paper_title: Capital Strategy 202627 - Updated format - WBC
findings.headline: Local Government Reorganisation from 2027/28 creates a one-year horizon within a five-year capital strategy.
findings.detail: The council is adopting strategies through 2031, but explicitly notes they are prepared 'as-is' because major structural reorganisation is coming in 2027/28. This means capital commitments made now may need to be restructured or revisited when the council's structure changes. The paper does not set out what that reorganisation entails or how the strategies will adapt to it.
findings.matters: A lender funding this council's capital programme needs to understand that strategic planning beyond 2027/28 is provisional, and any capital commitments with long payback periods face uncertainty from structural change. A finance director needs to know the time horizon for these strategies is compressed to one year of certainty.
findings.figures: LGR from 2027/28; strategies written for 2026-2031 (five years, but only one year of certainty).
findings.quote: These strategies have been prepared on an 'as-is' basis and will be subject to impacts from Local Government Reorganisation from 2027/28.

findings.paper_title: New Affordable Housing Delivery, Chiddingfold - Supplementary Budget Allocation
findings.headline: Detailed financial viability assessment for housing scheme withheld from public disclosure
findings.detail: Council states it has revisited financial appraisals for each site following cost increases, but results are contained in an exempt appendix. Details of how cost overruns affect scheme viability and rental income projections cannot be publicly assessed.
findings.matters: Rental income underpins debt service and scheme viability; exemption prevents external verification that revised scheme economics remain sound after cost overrun; viability concerns could emerge that were not disclosed
findings.figures: Viability assessment details not disclosed
findings.quote: Following an assessment of the revised costs, the financial appraisal for each of site has been revisited. A summary of the impact on the schemes' viability can be found in Exempt Appendix 1 of this report.

findings.paper_title: New Affordable Housing Delivery, Chiddingfold - Supplementary Budget Allocation
findings.headline: Homes England grant application pending; if declined, locks in £239,891 borrowing commitment
findings.detail: Council has applied to Homes England's Affordable Homes Programme for grant funding that would eliminate the borrowing requirement. Decision was anticipated in December 2025, but outcome is not reported. If unsuccessful, council proceeds with £240k borrowing.
findings.matters: Grant outcome determines whether borrowing is actually necessary; council is conditionally committing to debt pending external decision; payback period is 45 years without grant, 41 years if grant received
findings.figures: £239,891 borrowing eliminated if grant approved; payback period 45 years current, 41 years if grant received
findings.quote: If the Council is successful in securing an allocation, this will reduce the average payback period from 45 years to 41 years.

findings.paper_title: New Affordable Housing Delivery, Chiddingfold - Supplementary Budget Allocation
findings.headline: Project contingency exhausted by utility company delays beyond council control
findings.detail: Thames Water and UK Power Networks delays, plus unforeseen utility process requirements, have consumed the scheme's contingency allocation entirely. Contractor has submitted extension of time and cost claims exceeding the approved contingency, leaving no buffer for further issues.
findings.matters: Depleted contingency means remaining 24 homes at risk with no financial cushion for additional utility delays, weather, or unforeseen issues; project completion by March 2026 now depends on no further complications
findings.figures: Contingency fully consumed; 24 homes remaining; expected completion March 2026
findings.quote: This request for additional costs, which will increase the projected Final Account and includes Extensions of Time, exceeds the contingency allocated to the programme in the approved budget.

findings.paper_title: New Affordable Housing Delivery, Chiddingfold - Supplementary Budget Allocation
findings.headline: Council requires £239,891 additional borrowing to complete Chiddingfold affordable housing scheme
findings.detail: The original £9.3m budget approved in December 2022 is being exceeded. Supplementary budget of £481,880 is approved, funded by £241,990 from commuted sums and £239,891 from new borrowing. Two of 26 homes completed; remaining 24 expected by March 2026.
findings.matters: Council is taking on new debt to complete a capital scheme; the 5% cost overrun and utility-driven delays signal external factors the council cannot control affecting project viability
findings.figures: £481,880 supplementary budget; £239,891 new borrowing; original approved budget £9,305,046
findings.quote: That the Council resolves to approve the allocation of the supplementary budget of £481,880 to complete the delivery of the homes across the five sites in Chiddingfold, to be funded as follows £241,990 from Commuted Sums £239,891 from borrowing

findings.paper_title: Motion 3 - Securing the Financial Sustainability of West Surrey and Protecting Waverley Residents - Cllr Follows
findings.headline: Government has been given an overly optimistic financial position for the unitary authorities by Surrey County Council and partners
findings.detail: The motion asserts that Surrey County Council and its partners submitted an overly optimistic financial picture to government as part of the submission to create two unitary authorities. This risks undermining the new authority's financial sustainability before it even exists.
findings.matters: If the new unitary authority's financial projections are unrealistic, it will face immediate and material financial distress once established, creating risks for service delivery and the council's borrowing capacity.
findings.figures: None specified
findings.quote: The Government has been presented with an overly optimistic financial position by Surrey County Council and their partners in their submission to create two unitary authorities. This situation has the potential to undermine the new authority's financial sustainability before it even exists.

findings.paper_title: Motion 3 - Securing the Financial Sustainability of West Surrey and Protecting Waverley Residents - Cllr Follows
findings.headline: Constituent councils have significant and growing budget gaps; Spelthorne has a £11m gap in the current financial year
findings.detail: The motion highlights that many boroughs and districts forming the new West Surrey unitary authority have significant, growing year-on-year budget gaps. Spelthorne is cited as a specific example with a £11m budget gap in the current financial year.
findings.matters: These budget gaps in constituent councils represent structural financial weakness that will be absorbed into the new unitary, materially affecting its fiscal viability and borrowing capacity.
findings.figures: Spelthorne: £11m budget gap in this financial year
findings.quote: Many councils have significant (and growing) budget gaps year-on-year. Spelthorne, for example, has a budget gap of £11m in this financial year.

findings.paper_title: Appointment of Joint Strategic Director of Finance & Resources (S151 Officer)
findings.headline: Limited external candidate pool for senior finance role despite wide recruitment
findings.detail: The role was advertised widely from 23 October to 3 November 2025 across Jobs Go Public, LinkedIn, and LG Jobs. Of 48 applications received (1 internal, 6 from Jobs Go Public, 41 from LinkedIn), only the internal candidate was deemed suitable after screening and interview.
findings.matters: Inability to attract qualified external candidates for a senior financial leadership position may reflect local authority labour market conditions or role competitiveness.
findings.figures: 48 applications; 31 screened; 1 shortlisted (the internal candidate)
findings.quote: All candidates were screened and those meeting the initial criteria were interviewed by Talent Acquisition. Following on from these interviews, no other candidate was deemed suitable for the role.

findings.paper_title: Appointment of Joint Strategic Director of Finance & Resources (S151 Officer)
findings.headline: S151 Officer replaced following Richard Bates's resignation
findings.detail: The previous Joint Strategic Director of Finance & Resources has resigned. The role has been filled by internal promotion of Jo Knight, current Joint Assistant Director of Finance. Knight is CIPFA and CIMA qualified with over two years' experience as Deputy S151 Officer. The Joint Senior Staff Committee unanimously recommended the appointment on 21 November 2025.
findings.matters: A change in the finance director role signals continuity or discontinuity of financial leadership; an internal promotion on short notice could indicate either bench strength or pressure to fill the position quickly.
findings.figures: Appointment effective following full council approval on 2 and 9 December 2025
findings.quote: Due to the resignation of Richard Bates, Joint Strategic Director of Finance & Resources (Section 151 Officer), a replacement permanent appointment is required to ensure that both Councils meet their statutory requirements.

findings.paper_title: Wey Court EastBudget_October2025 COUNCIL
findings.headline: Construction cost overruns driven by unknown building conditions and structural failures uncovered during works
findings.detail: Cost uplifts totalling £453,710 arose from unknown conditions revealed when stripping the building, failure of existing roof sections, and contractor extension of time claims. The council's Quantity Surveyor deemed these costs fair and reasonable, but the defects indicate gaps in initial condition assessment.
findings.matters: Hidden building defects and poor pre-tender condition assessments suggest project planning and due diligence weaknesses, which affect confidence in the council's ability to manage future capital schemes.
findings.figures: £453,710 total cost uplift from unknown conditions and delays
findings.quote: The project has seen cost uplifts related to unknown conditions revealed upon stripping out the building, failure of the older parts of the existing roof, and valid extensions of time claims.

findings.paper_title: Wey Court EastBudget_October2025 COUNCIL
findings.headline: Project payback period extended from 28 to 31 years due to cost uplifts
findings.detail: The business case payback period has lengthened from 28 to 31 years as a result of the cost overruns, despite additional external funding received. This extends the council's capital recovery timeline and reduces the annual return on its investment.
findings.matters: Extended payback periods indicate deteriorating returns on capital investment and lengthen exposure to lease/income dependency, affecting long-term value for money.
findings.figures: Payback period adjusted from 28 to 31 years
findings.quote: The impact on the business case, when including the additional income secured for the project, means the payback period is adjusted from 28 to 31 years.

findings.paper_title: Wey Court EastBudget_October2025 COUNCIL
findings.headline: Wey Court East project £453,710 over budget, requiring £281,404 drawdown from General Fund working balance
findings.detail: The approved project budget was £5,607,719 but the projected final cost is now £6,061,421. Of the £453,710 shortfall, £172,306 will be funded from additional rent income and Surrey Empty Homes funding, leaving £281,404 to be drawn from the council's Revenue Account Reserve. This represents a 8.1% cost overrun requiring reserve depletion.
findings.matters: Reserve drawdown for capital project overruns reduces financial resilience and flexibility, a key metric lenders use to assess creditworthiness and the council's ability to manage unexpected pressures.
findings.figures: Total approved budget £5,607,719; projected cost £6,061,421; shortfall £453,710; reserve drawdown £281,404; additional income £172,306
findings.quote: The projected cost of this project now stands at £6,061,421 (excluding the original purchase cost). This gives a projected shortfall in budget of £453,710.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 4- Waverley Audit Findings (ISA 260) Report 24 25 Issued for comments 25 Sept
findings.headline: One transaction was miscoded, with income for 2025/26 recorded as 2024/25 revenue, requiring additional audit procedures to confirm no material impact
findings.detail: During income classification testing, auditors found one instance where income relating to the following year was incorrectly classified in the current year. Management undertook additional procedures to gain assurance that current-year revenue was not materially misstated. Management has committed to implementing enhanced review procedures at year-end.
findings.matters: Revenue miscoding can distort year-end income figures. Even isolated errors indicate that transaction controls around period allocation could be tighter, which matters to finance directors and auditors assessing financial statement reliability.
findings.figures: One instance of period misclassification identified
findings.quote: As part of our income classification testing, we note one instance where income relating to 2025/26 was incorrectly classified as income within 2024/25.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 4- Waverley Audit Findings (ISA 260) Report 24 25 Issued for comments 25 Sept
findings.headline: Five assets remain in use despite being fully depreciated, with a combined gross book value of £173.8k, indicating asset review processes are not working effectively
findings.detail: Audit testing identified 5 assets with nil net book values that are still operational, signalling that asset useful lives are not being reviewed regularly before assets become fully depreciated. The council's process for assessing and updating asset useful lives needs strengthening. Additionally, one group asset has not been revalued within the required 5-year cycle.
findings.matters: Unreviewed fully-depreciated assets in use suggest asset management controls could fail to catch larger issues, affecting balance sheet accuracy and the reliability of asset valuation—both material to lender assessment of financial position.
findings.figures: 5 assets at nil net book value; £173.8k total gross book value; one asset outside 5-year revaluation cycle
findings.quote: As part of our testing, we note 5 assets with nil net book values that were still in use. The total gross book value of these assets was £173.8k. The current asset values do not accurately represent their value in use.

news_drafts.headline: Housing Ombudsman found one case of severe maladministration and five service failures
news_drafts.lead: Multiple maladministration findings and one severe finding indicate systemic service delivery issues in housing (a material council function), with financial exposure to compensation claims.

news_drafts.headline: Local Government Reorganisation creates acknowledged risk of failure to deliver corporate objectives
news_drafts.lead: Organizational restructuring with a 9-month transition creates delivery risk and resource uncertainty during a critical financial period; lenders need clarity on how the authority will maintain service and financial delivery through the transition.

news_drafts.headline: External auditor recommends Council expand savings programmes to address budget pressures
news_drafts.lead: An external auditor's recommendation to expand savings programmes indicates the Council's current financial plan may not fully address underlying structural imbalances.
